children: China's home prices continued to fall at a similar pace in August, remaining a key drag on the world's second-largest economy.

Home prices in 70 major Chinese cities dropped 0.17% in August from July, compared with July's 0.18% decline, according to calculations by The Wall Street Journal based on data from the National Bureau of Statistics on Tuesday.
Of the 70 cities, 49 reported declines in prices from the preceding month, the data showed.

When compared with a year earlier, home prices in these cities fell 3.3% in August, narrowing slightly from a 3.4% drop in July. Among them, 65 cities reported a year-over-year price declines in August.
In the first eight months of the year, home prices fell 3.5% on year.
China's property slump showed no sign of recovery, despite incremental government measures to ease home purchase restrictions, mortgage rules and down payment requirements.
